MC	<p>9f80_da7a</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a42b31;">Gene K</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #a42b31;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a42b31;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e5b;">Gene N</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006e5b;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e5b;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #335ba7;">Gene X</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #335ba7;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #335ba7;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Progeny<br/>Count</th></tr><tr> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><span style="font-size: medium;">1</span></td> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, knx, +++, knx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>0a27_1b03</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #626219;">Gene A</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #626219;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #626219;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006b6f;">Gene F</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006b6f;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006b6f;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #5549be;">Gene H</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #5549be;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #5549be;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Progeny<br/>Count</th></tr><tr> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><span style="font-size: medium;">1</span></td> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, afh, +++, afh"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>9026_a554</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #85500a;">Gene A</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #85500a;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #85500a;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006b6f;">Gene B</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #006b6f;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006b6f;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8d3488;">Gene H</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #8d3488;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8d3488;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Progeny<br/>Count</th></tr><tr> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><span style="font-size: medium;">1</span></td> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, abh, +++, abh"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>bbd4_094e</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #00703b;">Gene C</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #00703b;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00703b;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1d6491;">Gene F</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #1d6491;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1d6491;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #993261;">Gene R</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #993261;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>8150_3d0f</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #904622;">Gene B</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #904622;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #904622;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00703b;">Gene C</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #00703b;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00703b;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1d6491;">Gene E</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #1d6491;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1d6491;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Progeny<br/>Count</th></tr><tr> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><span style="font-size: medium;">1</span></td> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, bce, +++, bce"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>0fe1_032d</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #85500a;">Gene E</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #85500a;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #85500a;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00703b;">Gene F</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #00703b;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00703b;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1d6491;">Gene H</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #1d6491;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1d6491;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Progeny<br/>Count</th></tr><tr> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><span style="font-size: medium;">1</span></td> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, efh, +++, efh"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>092f_8fff</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #626219;">Gene D</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #626219;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #626219;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006b6f;">Gene J</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006b6f;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006b6f;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8d3488;">Gene T</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #8d3488;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>d83d_5f0a</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #85500a;">Gene A</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #85500a;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #85500a;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00703b;">Gene E</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #00703b;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00703b;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #5549be;">Gene H</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #5549be;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #5549be;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Progeny<br/>Count</th></tr><tr> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><span style="font-size: medium;">1</span></td> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, aeh, +++, aeh"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #904622;">Gene B</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #904622;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #904622;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #436b17;">Gene H</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #436b17;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #436b17;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #763fa5;">Gene Y</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #763fa5;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #763fa5;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Progeny<br/>Count</th></tr><tr> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><span style="font-size: medium;">1</span></td> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, bhy, +++, bhy"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>0656_c05e</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a42b31;">Gene C</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #a42b31;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a42b31;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #626219;">Gene K</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #626219;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #626219;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1d6491;">Gene N</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #1d6491;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>6a8a_88ae</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #626219;">Gene A</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #626219;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #626219;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1d6491;">Gene J</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #1d6491;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1d6491;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8d3488;">Gene R</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #8d3488;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8d3488;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Progeny<br/>Count</th></tr><tr> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><span style="font-size: medium;">1</span></td> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, ajr, +++, ajr"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #00703b;">Gene K</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #00703b;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00703b;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1d6491;">Gene N</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #1d6491;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1d6491;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #993261;">Gene P</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #993261;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #993261;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Progeny<br/>Count</th></tr><tr> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><span style="font-size: medium;">1</span></td> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, knp, +++, knp"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>45c0_35bc</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #904622;">Gene B</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #904622;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #904622;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006b6f;">Gene C</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #006b6f;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006b6f;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #763fa5;">Gene W</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #763fa5;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>c246_d4d4</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #626219;">Gene A</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #626219;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #626219;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1b687d;">Gene F</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #1b687d;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1b687d;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #993261;">Gene M</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #993261;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #993261;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Progeny<br/>Count</th></tr><tr> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><span style="font-size: medium;">1</span></td> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, afm, +++, afm"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>8705_4265</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #904622;">Gene K</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #904622;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #904622;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006b6f;">Gene R</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #006b6f;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006b6f;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #763fa5;">Gene X</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #763fa5;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #763fa5;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Progeny<br/>Count</th></tr><tr> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><span style="font-size: medium;">1</span></td> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, krx, +++, krx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>b5ee_bd5c</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #85500a;">Gene A</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #85500a;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #85500a;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e5b;">Gene B</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #006e5b;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e5b;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8d3488;">Gene M</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #8d3488;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8d3488;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Progeny<br/>Count</th></tr><tr> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><span style="font-size: medium;">1</span></td> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, abm, +++, abm"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>86db_49bd</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #904622;">Gene J</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #904622;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #904622;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e5b;">Gene M</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006e5b;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e5b;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #335ba7;">Gene T</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #335ba7;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #335ba7;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Progeny<br/>Count</th></tr><tr> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><span style="font-size: medium;">1</span></td> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, jmt, +++, jmt"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #904622;">Gene D</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #904622;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #904622;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e5b;">Gene E</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #006e5b;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e5b;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #335ba7;">Gene F</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #335ba7;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #335ba7;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Progeny<br/>Count</th></tr><tr> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><span style="font-size: medium;">1</span></td> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, def, +++, def"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>c469_1fa2</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #85500a;">Gene C</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #85500a;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #85500a;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e5b;">Gene N</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #006e5b;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e5b;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #5549be;">Gene Y</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #5549be;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>3baa_f8de</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a42b31;">Gene C</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #a42b31;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a42b31;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #626219;">Gene N</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #626219;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #626219;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1d6491;">Gene P</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #1d6491;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1d6491;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Progeny<br/>Count</th></tr><tr> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><span style="font-size: medium;">1</span></td> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, cnp, +++, cnp"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #765900;">Gene A</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #765900;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #765900;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1b687d;">Gene H</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #1b687d;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1b687d;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #993261;">Gene X</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #993261;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>32cc_a076</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #436b17;">Gene M</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #436b17;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #436b17;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1d6491;">Gene R</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #1d6491;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1d6491;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8d3488;">Gene W</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #8d3488;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>e8b9_e4f0</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a42b31;">Gene J</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #a42b31;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a42b31;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00703b;">Gene N</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #00703b;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00703b;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #5549be;">Gene P</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #5549be;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #5549be;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Progeny<br/>Count</th></tr><tr> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><span style="font-size: medium;">1</span></td> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, jnp, +++, jnp"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #436b17;">Gene M</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #436b17;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #436b17;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1d6491;">Gene R</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #1d6491;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1d6491;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #993261;">Gene T</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #993261;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #993261;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Progeny<br/>Count</th></tr><tr> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><span style="font-size: medium;">1</span></td> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, mrt, +++, mrt"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>60d5_ec60</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a42b31;">Gene D</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #a42b31;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a42b31;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #626219;">Gene E</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #626219;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #626219;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006b6f;">Gene T</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #006b6f;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>a3b3_56cd</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a42b31;">Gene D</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #a42b31;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a42b31;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e5b;">Gene E</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #006e5b;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e5b;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #335ba7;">Gene T</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #335ba7;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #335ba7;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Progeny<br/>Count</th></tr><tr> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><span style="font-size: medium;">1</span></td> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, det, +++, det"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #904622;">Gene B</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #904622;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #904622;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00703b;">Gene H</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #00703b;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00703b;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1d6491;">Gene Y</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #1d6491;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1d6491;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Progeny<br/>Count</th></tr><tr> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><span style="font-size: medium;">1</span></td> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, bhy, +++, bhy"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>5cb1_4f12</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #765900;">Gene E</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #765900;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #765900;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e5b;">Gene F</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #006e5b;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e5b;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #5549be;">Gene K</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #5549be;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>32eb_45aa</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #436b17;">Gene H</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #436b17;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #436b17;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1d6491;">Gene M</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #1d6491;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1d6491;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8d3488;">Gene N</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #8d3488;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8d3488;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Progeny<br/>Count</th></tr><tr> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><span style="font-size: medium;">1</span></td> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, hmn, +++, hmn"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>236f_086c</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a42b31;">Gene H</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #a42b31;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a42b31;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00703b;">Gene M</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #00703b;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00703b;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #335ba7;">Gene W</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #335ba7;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #335ba7;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Progeny<br/>Count</th></tr><tr> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><span style="font-size: medium;">1</span></td> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, hmw, +++, hmw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>5af6_b8db</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #765900;">Gene C</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #765900;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #765900;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e5b;">Gene K</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #006e5b;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e5b;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #335ba7;">Gene M</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #335ba7;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #335ba7;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Progeny<br/>Count</th></tr><tr> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><span style="font-size: medium;">1</span></td> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, ckm, +++, ckm"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>6353_173f</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a42b31;">Gene E</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #a42b31;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a42b31;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e5b;">Gene H</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #006e5b;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e5b;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #5549be;">Gene Y</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #5549be;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #5549be;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Progeny<br/>Count</th></tr><tr> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><span style="font-size: medium;">1</span></td> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, ehy, +++, ehy"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>a612_1353</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a42b31;">Gene D</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #a42b31;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a42b31;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #626219;">Gene K</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #626219;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #626219;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #5549be;">Gene X</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #5549be;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #5549be;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Progeny<br/>Count</th></tr><tr> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><span style="font-size: medium;">1</span></td> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, dkx, +++, dkx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>2644_58ea</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #85500a;">Gene C</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #85500a;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #85500a;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00703b;">Gene P</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #00703b;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00703b;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #335ba7;">Gene Y</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #335ba7;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>c7d5_667f</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #904622;">Gene A</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #904622;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #904622;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #436b17;">Gene M</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #436b17;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #436b17;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #5549be;">Gene Y</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #5549be;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #5549be;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Progeny<br/>Count</th></tr><tr> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><span style="font-size: medium;">1</span></td> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, amy, +++, amy"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a42b31;">Gene A</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #a42b31;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a42b31;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #436b17;">Gene K</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #436b17;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #436b17;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1d6491;">Gene X</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #1d6491;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1d6491;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Progeny<br/>Count</th></tr><tr> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><span style="font-size: medium;">1</span></td> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, akx, +++, akx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>3ef2_127e</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #85500a;">Gene E</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #85500a;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #85500a;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1b687d;">Gene W</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #1b687d;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1b687d;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8d3488;">Gene Y</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #8d3488;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8d3488;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Progeny<br/>Count</th></tr><tr> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><span style="font-size: medium;">1</span></td> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, ewy, +++, ewy"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #765900;">Gene D</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #765900;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #765900;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e5b;">Gene P</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006e5b;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e5b;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #763fa5;">Gene X</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #763fa5;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #763fa5;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Progeny<br/>Count</th></tr><tr> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><span style="font-size: medium;">1</span></td> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, dpx, +++, dpx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>5885_475b</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #904622;">Gene H</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #904622;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #904622;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006b6f;">Gene M</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #006b6f;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006b6f;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #5549be;">Gene P</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #5549be;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #5549be;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Progeny<br/>Count</th></tr><tr> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><span style="font-size: medium;">1</span></td> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, hmp, +++, hmp"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>1e62_7cf4</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #436b17;">Gene C</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #436b17;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #436b17;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1b687d;">Gene X</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #1b687d;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1b687d;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #763fa5;">Gene Y</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #763fa5;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype.
