MC	<p>328b_2a63</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #904622;">Gene F</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #904622;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #904622;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00703b;">Gene N</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #00703b;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00703b;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #5549be;">Gene Y</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #5549be;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #5549be;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Progeny<br/>Count</th></tr><tr> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><span style="font-size: medium;">1</span></td> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, fny, +++, fny"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #85500a;">Gene D</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #85500a;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #85500a;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1b687d;">Gene E</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #1b687d;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1b687d;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #763fa5;">Gene N</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #763fa5;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #763fa5;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Progeny<br/>Count</th></tr><tr> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><span style="font-size: medium;">1</span></td> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, den, +++, den"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>c4f5_bc24</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #904622;">Gene M</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #904622;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #904622;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00703b;">Gene W</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #00703b;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00703b;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1d6491;">Gene X</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #1d6491;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>27e9_d575</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #904622;">Gene C</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #904622;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #904622;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00703b;">Gene J</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #00703b;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00703b;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #763fa5;">Gene X</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #763fa5;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #763fa5;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Progeny<br/>Count</th></tr><tr> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><span style="font-size: medium;">1</span></td> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, cjx, +++, cjx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>0bca_bbb9</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a42b31;">Gene D</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #a42b31;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a42b31;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #436b17;">Gene M</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #436b17;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #436b17;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #335ba7;">Gene Y</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #335ba7;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #335ba7;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Progeny<br/>Count</th></tr><tr> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><span style="font-size: medium;">1</span></td> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, dmy, +++, dmy"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>c917_e45f</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a42b31;">Gene K</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #a42b31;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a42b31;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #436b17;">Gene P</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #436b17;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #436b17;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #335ba7;">Gene T</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #335ba7;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>e3f7_93c6</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #626219;">Gene K</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #626219;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #626219;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006b6f;">Gene N</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #006b6f;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006b6f;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #5549be;">Gene Y</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #5549be;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #5549be;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Progeny<br/>Count</th></tr><tr> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><span style="font-size: medium;">1</span></td> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, kny, +++, kny"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a42b31;">Gene B</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #a42b31;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a42b31;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #436b17;">Gene E</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #436b17;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #436b17;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1d6491;">Gene Y</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #1d6491;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1d6491;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Progeny<br/>Count</th></tr><tr> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><span style="font-size: medium;">1</span></td> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, bey, +++, bey"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>8296_c474</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #765900;">Gene E</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #765900;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #765900;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e5b;">Gene F</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006e5b;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e5b;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #993261;">Gene T</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #993261;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>1923_1f17</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #85500a;">Gene B</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #85500a;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #85500a;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00703b;">Gene C</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #00703b;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00703b;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #335ba7;">Gene M</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #335ba7;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #335ba7;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Progeny<br/>Count</th></tr><tr> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><span style="font-size: medium;">1</span></td> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, bcm, +++, bcm"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral.
